title: look-alike-controls "a look-alike drove a Harbour control" failed once in a parallel local run (not reproduced)
description:
## Problem

While finishing LIN-4104 (PR #2225), one local run of the related run-control E2E set (102 specs, several workers) failed `look-alike-controls` "a look-alike drove a Harbour control": a `GET /api/dispatch/preview` (read-only) was recorded during the look-alike clicks. Re-run in isolation: 4/4 pass; the whole file passes; CI on every head of the PR was green, and main is green on `4a0d90ee`. It did not reproduce.

## Why it matters

The spec guards that ticket text cannot act as a Harbour control (LIN-3385/LIN-3401). A flake there either hides a real regression or teaches people to ignore the guard. Low priority because one failure in many runs has not reproduced.

## Acceptance

* Either a reproduction with a cause (for example a preview fetch from the page's own poll landing inside the click window) and a fix, or a decision that the spec should ignore read-only `GET` calls and say why.
* No change to what the spec asserts about look-alike POSTs/dispatches.

## Anchors

* `tests/e2e/look-alike-controls.spec.js` (the "a look-alike drove a Harbour control" test and how it records requests).
* `GET /api/dispatch/preview` callers in `public/prompt-section.js`.

## Unvalidated idea

The preview is a read the opened box makes on its own; filter recorded requests to non-GET, or wait for the box's preview to settle before clicking.

Priority low (1): one non-reproduced failure, no product impact seen. Related: LIN-4104.

## Resolution

Fixed in PR #2255 ([https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2255](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2255>)), merged as `00c6261b`: `/test/set-local-session` starts the worker key's held task facts over (and clears the issues memo), so a reseed no longer inherits the previous spec's set and refresh floor. The spec's assertions are unchanged and GETs are not filtered. Regression spec: `tests/e2e/lin-4110-reseed-held-facts.spec.js`. Cause, review and close-out are in the comment trail; the pre-close description is kept in the task snapshots. Follow-up: LIN-4160.

comments.body: Seen again during LIN-4119 (PR #2229, S3a-2): `look-alike-controls` also fails in **full** E2E runs on `main` (not only in parallel local runs) and passes alone on both main and the PR branch. Same finding as this ticket, so it is not filed twice; linked as related to LIN-4119. Worth weighing when you pick this up: the failure looks load/ordering-dependent rather than random, which may make it reproducible with the full suite.

**New evidence (3 Nov), raising priority to High at John's call.** This is no longer a single unreproduced failure:

- **It cost a production deploy.** On `main` at `300c811f` (LIN-4106's merge), E2E shard 2/4 failed `look-alike-controls.spec.js:209` on all three attempts: a read-only `GET …/dispatch/preview?promptName=autopilot&surface=task` was seen during the look-alike clicks. Railway's deploy waits for green CI, so `300c811f` didn't deploy. A re-run of the job went green, but that didn't trigger a deploy, and the UI round stalled for about 3 hours until a manual redeploy.
- **Builders keep hitting it.** LIN-4106's builder logged it as "the known flake" in its baseline and final runs (it passes when re-run alone, and fails under parallel load).
- **The same family of problem:** LIN-4113's builder named E2E state shared between specs as its single biggest cost ("failed in 7 of 8 full runs"; per-account remembered team leaking between specs), on its "Survey spike 1a" comment.

Goal: the spec is reliable under the suite's normal parallel load, without weakening what it guards (that ticket text cannot drive a Harbour control).

## Investigation: cause confirmed, reproduced every time

**Cause:** state shared between specs, not randomness and not the look-alike. The server's held task-facts set (`lib/task-facts-holder.js`, one entry per `urlKey`) outlives `/test/set-local-session`. Every spec in a Playwright worker uses the same key (`local-workspace-w<N>`). When an earlier spec in that worker has already filled the set (with its own tasks) and used up the refresh's **60 s attempt floor** (`ATTEMPT_FLOOR_MS`), this spec's reseeded `LOCAL-LA1` is missing from the set. Every `/state` read then answers `incomplete: 'task-missing'` until a minute has passed. `public/prompt-section.js` (`acceptStateRead`, then `rereadUntilComplete`) re-reads the state every 1 s while it is incomplete, and **each re-read calls `refreshRunPreview()`**. So `GET …/dispatch/preview?promptName=autopilot&surface=task` fires about 1 s after load, which lands inside the spec's 500 ms click window. The look-alike never drove anything.

### Evidence
- **CI trace** (run 41600882212 attempt 1, shard 2/4, `300c811f`, artifact `playwright-report-shard-2`, `…-retry1/trace.zip`). Both `/state` bodies are `{"incomplete":"task-missing", …}`. Timeline: state read at +0 ms, then preview; clicks at about +700 ms; second state read at +1057 ms, then the offending preview 19 ms later, still inside the 500 ms wait. It failed all three attempts because the retries were also inside the floor.
- **Local repro, deterministic:**
  - `npx playwright test tests/e2e/lin-3975-task-run.spec.js tests/e2e/look-alike-controls.spec.js --workers=1` fails with the exact CI signature.
  - `look-alike-controls.spec.js` alone: 3/3 pass.
- **Decisive experiment** (temporary probe of `/state` before the page load, same ordering):
  - No wait: probe reads `task-missing`, and the test fails.
  - Wait 62 s (past the floor) before the page load: the probe's kick can then refresh, and **12/12 pass**.
  - This tells the floor/held-set cause apart from "load" or "the page's own poll timing" alone.
- **Prior instance of the same class:** LIN-4120 (`d01d5a0c`). A remembered team leaked across specs, so the holder refused writes and answered `task-missing` for TEST-13. It was fixed per describe. LIN-4113's "E2E state shared between specs" cost is the same family.

### Acceptance witness
The spec's own assertion tracks the real outcome once the shared state is removed: the only offender ever recorded was the page's own re-read preview. **Ignoring GETs is rejected:** several guards in `FORBIDDEN` are GET-only signals of a look-alike driving a control. Examples are `fake-pr-state-url` (the PR-state poll reading a hostile `data-pr-state-url`), `/brief?` and `/recap?` (panels mounted from hostile `.sess-ctx-panel`). Filtering GETs would blind exactly those. Waiting in the spec for the preview to "settle" doesn't fix it either: with the floor held, the re-read loop runs for 15 s.

### Proposed fix (at the seam, for the whole class)
`/test/set-local-session` starts the key's held set over from the new seed, before any page reads it. It waits out an in-flight refresh, invalidates the entry, forgets that key's attempt floor, and runs one urgent refresh to completion. This needs two small seams on the refresh (`forget(urlKey)`, `inFlightFor(urlKey)`), test-only callers. It fixes any spec whose reseed follows another spec on the same worker key, not just this one. The spec's assertions are unchanged.

**PR #2255** (https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2255), commit `1d497704`, for review, not merged:
- Failing ordering: 12/12 pass, run twice.
- Unit suite: 22,559/22,559 pass (new holder test included).
- Full local E2E (4 workers): 1,981 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed. The one failure is `live-console.spec.js:444` (lc-pulse width 334 vs 319). It fails identically with the change stashed, so it is a local layout difference, unrelated, and green on CI.
- CI on the PR is pending.

### Siblings / not in scope
- `_workspaceIssuesMemo` (`server.js`, 30 s, keyed by workspace id) is the same class: per-key server state that outlives a reseed. Lower risk (two read-only drilldown routes, explicit `/test/clear-workspace-issues-memo` already used). It could also be cleared on reseed; left for review.
- Product note, not the cause: on an incomplete state answer, `prompt-section.js` re-fires an identical preview read on each of up to 15 re-reads. Previewing only when the step/choice changes would save requests. Separate improvement.

## Review — LIN-4110

Reviewed **PR #2255** (https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2255) at head `1d497704` (base `300c811f`, which is current `main`).

CI: green on head `1d497704`. Run 41630123134: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and `CI success` all passed.

### Scope against the plan
The diff matches the fix proposed in the investigation comment, and touches only those places: `refresh.forget` / `refresh.inFlightFor` in `lib/task-facts-holder.js`, `resetTaskFactsForTest` in `server.js`, one call in `/test/set-local-session` (`routes/test.js`), and one unit test. The spec's assertions are unchanged (`look-alike-controls.spec.js` is not in the diff), and GETs are not filtered. Both acceptance points hold. The cause is fixed at the reseed, not hidden in the spec.

### Regression check
`git log -30` on the four files: the related earlier fixes are LIN-4120 (`d9931859`, remembered team cleared on reseed) and LIN-4069/4070 (holder and refresh). Both are still in place. The new reset runs **after** the remembered-team clear, so the gate does not refuse its urgent refresh with `team`. Nothing reverted is applied again. None of the anchored files changed on `main` since the ticket was opened, apart from `300c811f`, which is the base.

### Verified independently (this review)
- **The failing order, PR branch:** `npx playwright test tests/e2e/lin-3975-task-run.spec.js tests/e2e/look-alike-controls.spec.js --workers=1` → **12/12 pass**.
  - Note: the first attempt silently reused **another workspace's** `node server.js` already listening on :3001 (`reuseExistingServer: !CI`), so it tested someone else's code. I re-ran on a private copy of the config with ports moved. Anyone verifying locally should check `lsof -iTCP:3001` first.
- **Mutation, e2e:** with the `resetTaskFacts(...)` call in `routes/test.js` disabled, the same order → **1 failed**: `look-alike-controls.spec.js:209` (task page), which is the CI signature. Reverted.
- **Mutation, unit:** with `refresh.forget` changed to a no-op → `lin-4069-task-facts-holder.test.js` **fails 1**. Restored → 24/24 pass. Reverted.
- **Error handling:** the refresh promise never rejects; a failed fetch resolves `{written:false, refusal:'failed'}`, so a fetch failure cannot fail the reseed route. `forget` runs again after the urgent refresh, so the page's own first urgent refresh is not blocked by the floor this reset just set. Single-flight is respected: the reset waits out an in-flight refresh before invalidating.
- **Security:** both new seams are reached only from `createTestRoutes`, which is mounted under `NODE_ENV === 'test'`. No production caller.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
**Class:** per-key server state held in memory that outlives `/test/set-local-session` on a per-worker key. That is this ticket's bounded class, as named in its investigation comment, with LIN-4120 as the earlier instance.
- Held task facts: handled by this PR.
- `_workspaceIssuesMemo` (`server.js:3105`): **inside**, see the ledger.
- A Home-pipeline `writeTaskFacts` landing after the reset: **inside**, see the ledger.
- The other module-level maps (`prFilesCache`, `prStateSharedCache`, `failOpenPrStatusCache`, `library` cache, token-refresh `inflight`) are keyed by PR, repo or credential, not by the seeded issue set, so they are outside this class. Nothing to file.
- The product note (prompt-section re-fires the same preview on each incomplete re-read) is a different problem: **outside**. Close-out should file it after checking it doesn't already exist.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside: no automated test pins "a reseed starts the held set over".** The only witness is a spec order (`lin-3975-task-run` then `look-alike-controls`, same worker), and CI's sharding does not guarantee that order. If the reset were removed, CI could stay green, which is how this bug got through before. **Settle before the merge (close-out makes this fix):** add `tests/e2e/lin-4110-reseed-held-facts.spec.js`.
  - Steps: `seedLocalWorkspace(page, seedA)` with task A, then `GET /workspace/${urlKey}/api/task/A/state` (this fills the held set and sets the 60 s floor). Then `seedLocalWorkspace(page, seedB)`, which adds task B, using the same `urlKey`. Then immediately `GET /workspace/${urlKey}/api/task/B/state`, and assert the body's `incomplete` is not `'task-missing'`.
  - The distinguishing condition: a second reseed inside 60 s of a read on the same key. Mutation check: it must go red with the `resetTaskFacts` call disabled.
- **Inside: `_workspaceIssuesMemo` survives a reseed** (30 s, keyed by workspace id; the id is deterministic per `urlKey`, so a reseed hits the earlier spec's entry). This is the same class. 17 e2e call sites already clear it by hand, and no failure has been seen. **Recommendation: do it here.** In `setLocalSession` (`routes/test.js`), next to the `resetTaskFacts` call, add `if (clearWorkspaceIssuesMemo) clearWorkspaceIssuesMemo();`. The memo is a pure cache, so clearing every key just makes other workers re-read correct data. If not done here, drop it with the reason "explicit per-spec clears already cover the two read-only drilldown routes". Do not file it.
- **Inside: "an older fetch cannot land after the reset" covers only the refresh trigger.** Home's pipeline writes the holder directly (`homePipelineDeps.writeTaskFacts`) and is not serialized by `inFlightFor`. A Home request from the previous spec that is still being processed could, in principle, write the old seed's set after the reset. No instance has been observed. The window is milliseconds after the previous spec's context closes, and the task page's urgent refresh recovers, since the floor was forgotten. **Recommendation: drop it with that reason**, and record the drop in the close-out comment.
- **Inside: reliability under the suite's normal parallel load** (the ticket's goal) is shown only by one green CI run plus the author's local runs. CI cannot show it isn't flaky. **Settle after the deploy (a monitor):** the next ~10 `main` CI runs show no `look-alike-controls.spec.js:209` failure, retries included (a pass on retry still counts as a failure here). It fails loudly in the E2E job. Only repeated runs can show it, because shard order varies.
- **Outside:** preview re-fired on each incomplete re-read in `public/prompt-section.js`. Close-out files it as a separate improvement.

Rollback: revert commit `1d497704` (test-harness only, no data shape change, fully reversible).

### Verdict
**Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger.** The cause is confirmed and fixed at the reseed. The fix is verified red-without and green-with on the failing order, and CI is green. Close-out must add the reseed regression spec (and the memo clear, or drop it with its reason) before merging.

## Close-out — LIN-4110

**Merged:** PR #2255 (https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2255), squash commit `00c6261b`, pinned to head `ba4e9fa9` with `--match-head-commit`. Review verdict was Approve, conditional on close-out discharging the ledger.

### Changes I made after the approval (each answers a review line)
- `ba4e9fa9` — **new `tests/e2e/lin-4110-reseed-held-facts.spec.js`** (review: "no automated test pins 'a reseed starts the held set over'"). Seed A with task A, read `/state` for A (fills the held set, uses the 60 s floor), reseed with the same key adding task B, then read B's `/state` straight away; it must not answer `incomplete: 'task-missing'`.
  - Mutation: with the `resetTaskFacts(...)` call in `routes/test.js` disabled, it **fails** ("task B is in the second seed; a held set from seed A would say task-missing"). With it restored, it passes. Both runs were on a private copy of the Playwright config with ports 3411–3413, because another workspace's server was listening on :3001 (the false-verification trap the review named).
- `ba4e9fa9` — **`_workspaceIssuesMemo` cleared on reseed** (`routes/test.js`, `if (clearWorkspaceIssuesMemo) clearWorkspaceIssuesMemo();` after the reset), as the review recommended. The memo is keyed by the local workspace's fixed id and is a pure cache.
- No citation or comment was made stale by these changes.
- Related specs on the new code (`lin-4110` new spec, `lin-3975-task-run`, `look-alike-controls`, `lin-4120-home-backlog`, `task-page`, `--workers=1`, private ports): 34/34 pass.

### Ledger
- **Inside: no test pinned the reseed reset** → done (spec above; red without the reset, green with it).
- **Inside: `_workspaceIssuesMemo` survives a reseed** → done (cleared on reseed, above).
- **Inside: a Home-pipeline `writeTaskFacts` landing after the reset** → **dropped, with the review's reason:** no instance observed; the window is milliseconds after the previous spec's context closes, and the task page's urgent refresh recovers because the floor was forgotten by the reset. Not filed.
- **Inside: reliability under normal parallel load** → named monitor, from the review: **the next ~10 `main` CI runs (E2E job) show no `look-alike-controls.spec.js:209` failure, retries included (a pass on retry counts as a failure).** It fails loudly in the E2E job. This is a claim that needs elapsed time, so it is on that monitor, not held here. Main CI run 41636568360 on `00c6261b` is the first of those and passed.
- **Outside: `prompt-section.js` re-fires the same preview on each incomplete re-read** → filed as **LIN-4160** (Improvement, `kind:follow-up`, priority Low: request hygiene with no user-visible defect; related link to this ticket). I searched first and found no existing ticket for it.
- **Outside (review): other module-level maps** (`prFilesCache`, `prStateSharedCache`, `failOpenPrStatusCache`, library cache, token-refresh `inflight`) are keyed by PR, repo or credential, not the seeded issue set. Nothing to file.
- **Rollback (named by review):** revert commit `00c6261b` (test-harness only, no data-shape change).

### CI
- Head `ba4e9fa9`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and `CI success` all passed before the merge (read after the push; the first read was empty and checks registered a moment later).
- `main` at `00c6261b`: Tests run 41636568360 passed.

### After the deploy
The deploy landed: the live site's footer links commit `00c6261b5b0097689dc816068a2e79c211784ca9`, the merge commit. The change is test-harness only (the new seams are reached only from `/test/set-local-session`, mounted under `NODE_ENV=test`), so there is no post-deploy check beyond main's passing CI on that commit, which includes the new spec. No post-deploy step was skipped.

### Tidying
- LIN-4104 and LIN-4119 (related) are already Done; nothing to change.
- Description: archived first (`GET /brief?noRefresh=1`, then `GET /snapshots` showed a snapshot with the identical description). It holds only the original problem, why it matters, acceptance, anchors and the original idea, with no plan, research or scoping sections to prune, so nothing was removed; a resolution stub was appended.
- The `Bug` label is left in place.

## Survey spike 1a (bug)

**1. Why was this difficult? Where did it bind?**
The fix was small (about 30 lines). Finding the cause was the hard part, and three things made it slow:
- **Two readers poll the same URL.** `public/task-page.js`'s poller and `public/prompt-section.js`'s `rereadUntilComplete` both read `/api/task/:id/state`, each at its own cadence. I could only tell which one sent the offending preview from timing in the CI trace: the preview followed one state read 19 ms later.
- **The cause was in test-harness state, not the page.** The held set is created in `server.js`. Its 60 s attempt floor lives inside a closure in `lib/task-facts-holder.js` with no way to reset it. `routes/test.js` was never given the holder.
- **Wiring meant editing `createTestRoutes`' 40-odd-parameter line** in both `server.js` and `routes/test.js`.
- **Resets are scattered.** "Reset this worker key" has no single home: the remembered team is reset inside `set-local-session` (LIN-4120), the issues memo has its own route, and each spec's `beforeEach` lists 6–8 `clear-*` calls by hand. Nothing failed loudly when one was missing.

The CI trace's response bodies (`task-missing`) were decisive. A local-only `live-console` failure was noise I ruled out with my change stashed.

**2. What would I have done first?**
One small consolidation: a single "reseed resets this worker key" seam that owns every per-urlKey server cache (held set and floor, remembered team, issues memo). That would have made this fix one line in a known place. LIN-4120 and this ticket would have been the same fix rather than two, and the next spec that hits it wouldn't need an investigation. Diagnosis would still need the trace; I'd guess it saves a third to a half of this ticket. The product code itself needed no tidy.

**3. What did the ticket get wrong?**
- **"Rare, not reproduced, load-dependent."** It was deterministic, and it depended on which spec ran just before on the same worker key, not on load. Running `lin-3975-task-run` then `look-alike-controls` in one worker failed every time.
- **Its unvalidated idea, filtering to non-GET,** would have blinded GET-only guards: `fake-pr-state-url`, `/brief?` and `/recap?`.
- **"Wait for the preview to settle"** fails too: while the floor holds, the re-read loop runs for 15 s.
- **The anchor** (preview callers in `prompt-section.js`) was the right symptom, but the cause was server-side state that outlived the reseed.
